notes.title: Update | Update | Update | Update
notes.content: [p]Gooood morning fellow Screw Drivers,[/p][p][/p][p]we have brought several small updates over the last couple of weeks, and we gotta admit that we were just a little bit too lazy to post the patchnotes for every one of them. But now it's time to fill you in on all the things that happened in the last couple of weeks leading up to the current version of [b]v0.5.4.25[/b]:[/p][p][/p][h2]Minor changes[/h2][list][*][p]In the general settings you can now enable or disable whether engines and gearboxes should provide or be provided with power through mounting holes.[/p][/*][*][p]We moved all spawn points of challenges slightly up again, so that hopefully, cars don't spawn inside the terrain or road anymore.[/p][/*][*][p]We also increased the time between the countdown numbers again. This way, the cars should have enough time to properly spawn and stand still, before the race starts.[/p][/*][*][p]We changed the power of the V engine from 78HP to 82HP.[/p][/*][*][p]You can directly jump from building to driving on the supersonic map again, by holding down the 'Return' key.[/p][/*][*][p]The start/finish checkpoint now has a beautiful checkered texture on the ground.[/p][/*][*][p]We tried to add the old dynamic camera mode again. Let us know if we did a good job. I did just copy over the code, but due to the changes in the camera system in general, it might still behave slightly different.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a new seat, the passenger seat. This way you can bulid busses or multiple seats in general, but still decide where the driver should sit. (In a later update, the passenger seats will be filled with passengers ;) )[/p][/*][*][p]The first person seat camera now moves a little, depending on the acceleration of the car.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now configure dead zones for controllers. This should help to counter stick drift. You can also see previews of the driving controls in the controls settings now.[/p][/*][*][p]You can switch back to the old menu layout in the general settings.[/p][/*][*][p]We added two new platformer challenges to Pulau Mahkota[/p][/*][*][p]You can now show the gear ratios on axles by pressing 'G' in the building editor.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Stunt Showdown (DLC)[/h2][list][*][p]The remaining time of stunt challenges has been missing in general. It should be shown again now.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug in Skate Park Heat, where the car always spawned under the map.[/p][/*][*][p]In Salto Bowl, the stunt area has been missing, and is now shown correctly again.[/p][/*][*][p]In the results panel, there was a missing translation that was visible for a short time before the animation started.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Pretty Fly (DLC)[/h2][list][*][p]There have been two challenges, where the order of checkpoints was wrong, where the last landing checkpoint was falsely the first checkpoint. This should now be in correct order again.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Bug fixes[/h2][list][*][p]There was a bug which prevented hinge joints directly mounted onto planetary gears to rotate. This should be fixed now.[/p][/*][*][p]The shadow quality settings are now applied when the game starts. You don't have to go to the settings menu and re-apply them anymore.[/p][/*][*][p]In the free camera mode, the scroll wheel was inverted. It should now work in the correct direction.[/p][/*][*][p]The unlock conditions in the tec tree sometimes weren't turning green, although they should be. This was due to rounding errors. Should now be fixed.[/p][/*][*][p]The camera in the building editor wasn't rotating correctly, especially when moving the mouse really fast. This should now be correct and feel a lot smoother.[/p][/*][*][p]Ignore steering angle did not have any effect. It should now.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the road in Trophy Run not having an underside.[/p][/*][*][p]Sometimes after playing a tutorial, the 'R' key stopped working to delete parts in the buliding editor. This is now fixed.[/p][/*][*][p]Sometimes when creating a new car, the game opened a rename panel, and got stuck there.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an exception when trying to rename the Favorites or All tab in the car categories.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed, that the FPS limit was not applied.[/p][/*][*][p]We moved all spawn points closer to the ground in races. So when starting races, you shouldn't fall down from that far up anymore.[/p][/*][*][p]When gaining gems at the end of a challenge, the animation has shown the wrong amount of gems. This is now fixed.[/p][/*][*][p]The chroma/sensa settings should now also automaticall be applied when the game starts.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some more water that clipped through the ground on Pulau Mahkota (probably haven't fixed every spot yet tho :D )[/p][/*][*][p]The Go Kart 2 wheels weren't included in the tec tree. Now they are.[/p][/*][*][p]It was possible to unlock parts by just satisfying the conditions, and then driving the challenge once. Now you actually have to beat the bronze time to unlock the parts.[/p][/*][*][p]When unlocking the racing wheels, they were colored weirdly. Now they keep their black rubber color.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug, where uploading vehicles to the workshop did not work, if the vehicle contained any DLC parts.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the UI in the building menu, since some texts were barely readable.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some environment in Tornanti Turbolenti[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the depth of field in the first person seat camera[/p][/*][*][p]We forgot to merge both the tec tree and ranklist career progress with the last update. This should be fixed now. All your gems, unlocked parts and challenges should now be restored.[/p][/*][*][p]Anti aliasing didn't work properly. This should now work, and you can configure it in the graphics settings. [/p][/*][*][p]The tec tree did show some parts to be locked, although they were already unlocked. Should be fixed.[/p][/*][*][p]Center of mass did not display for some vehicles.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the elo panels causing extreme lags.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed acceleration bug, where you could increase acceleration by both using keyboard and controller simultaneously to accelerate.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug, where some cars spawned below the map.[/p][/*][*][p]We adjusted some environment objects of races on Pulau Mahkota.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Multiplayer[/h2][list][*][p]Fixed resetting to checkpoint not working in multiplayer.[/p][/*][*][p]When one player doesn't load the vehicles of other players, the challenge then starts anyways. The player who hasn't loaded all vehicles then becomes a ghost for everybody, so there aren't any fault collisions.[/p][/*][*][p]In the graphics settings, you can now turn off the particles and VFX of other players.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the loading percentage in the multiplayer race loading screen always showing a non-changing number.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now disable the physics and colliders of other players in the general settings in multiplayer for better performance.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a problem, where you sometimes could not drive at the start of a race until going into reverse gear once. This should be fixed now.[/p][/*][*][p]Added small little white arrows at the bottom of the screen for other player cars that are right behind you.[/p][/*][*][p]Added meta information to multiplayer player list. Whenever a player crashes, repairs or resets, a little notification pops up.[/p][/*][*][p]When repairing or resetting, you now become a ghost for 6 seconds, so others can't crash into you.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now see the player names of other players above their cars.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]This should cover all that has happened in July :D[/p][p]Next up, we will finalize the multiplayer so you can also host your own servers. Give us a couple of weeks, and it should be ready![/p][p]And also, I hosted a test multiplayer server for the last couple of days or so. But I probably will have to shut it down over the next two weeks, since the server was running on my own PC, and I'm gonna go on some small vacation soon ;)[/p][p]Until then, happy and safe drive![/p][p]Marc & Simon[/p]

notes.title: New Update brings Major Performance Optimizations and countless Bug Fixes!
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/305944382f8786023d1f411935c5b7785bec4a86.png"][/img]

Happy Friday and welcome to the biggest performance optimization we ever did!

With this update, we reprogrammed and restructured the whole project from the ground up. We took our core systems like the building editor, the driving physics and the vehicle calculation, and reassembled them freshly. We also deleted all ancient assets that were still in the project, and we reimported all the assets that are actually included in the game.

All in all, we managed to reduce the RAM usage, increased FPS and reduced loading times by some margin. And most importantly, if the game did not start for you at all, now it might actually work!

We hope you enjoy this sleek new version of [b]Screw Drivers[/b]. Now that we got performance figured out, you can expect a lot of cool new features and content coming up next 🙂

And here are all the changes (hopefully, if I haven't forgotten any):[/p][p][/p][h3][b]General[/b][/h3][list][*][p]We completely reworked all menus and UI. The menus are now separate from each other, which means that the game sometimes has to load for some short time, but this reduces the total RAM usage of the game.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Building[/b][/h3][list][*][p]We completely reworked the X-menu. It now actually spawns your vehicle, which you can then actually test a little bit. This feature is still not finished, we plan to add more live telemetry data like suspension travel, live wind resistance, live downforce and so on.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Driving[/b][/h3][list][*][p]You can now view the minimap in fullscreen by pressing 'M'.[/p][/*][*][p]We reprogrammed all camera modes. They aren't perfect yet, so feel free to try them out and let us know, which one you like most so we can improve those even more.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Bug fixes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]When changing the keybinding of headlights, the car would not calculate. This should be fixed.[/p][/*][*][p]The green-gears bug should now finally be gone, but who knows, maybe it comes back some day?[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]And we fixed many many more bugs. I can't list them all, because some bugs just will be fixed because of the whole restructuring of the project. Any new bugs you encounter, please report them to us on discord, steam or by carrier pigeon.

Thank you all for playing Screw Drivers and for being part of the best community!
Simon & Marc

notes.title: Pretty Fly DLC, Racetrack Map and Physics Changes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/5c84b5618a7fd164229823ee28f2090b9ef97ec6.png[/img]

Gooood afternoon everybody, this one is a big one! ːsteamhappyː

After working day and night for the last two months, without any sleep or eating, we now have one of the biggest updates ever. And not only that, we also added airplanes to the game. Since the Steam Workshop is already flooded with airplanes, we finally added proper airplane physics to the game. With our new DLC “Pretty Fly” we added a huuuuuuge map to the game with airports and floating islands. You will have airplane wings, propellers and turbines to craft your own airplanes and challenge all the six monarchs of Pretty Fly:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3500960/Screw_Drivers__Pretty_Fly

If you rather wanna stay on the ground, we also released the huuuge “Rennpisten Insel” to the main game. It’s the biggest non-aircraft island ever, and it contains an immense amount of roads and racing challenges.

On top of all of that, there are a bunch of new building blocks, changes in downforce and physics, looots of bug fixed, some new bugs you can discover and some more changes.

We hope you enjoy all the new stuff, as always please let us know your thoughts and feedback on everything, be it in the Steam discussions, in the comments below or on discord. We’re happy if you’re happy, and we cannot wait to see you on the Rennpisten Insel or in the skies!

[b]So here is a list with all the additions/changes/fixes that come with the update:[/b]



[h3][b]Rennpisten Insel (German for “Island of great and big race tracks suited for high speeds and excellently engineered race cars“)[/b][/h3]
[list][*] The new island is finally here! With the Rennpisten Insel we added a huge new island with a million kilometers of roads. There is a lot to discover, all roads have dedicated and special names, the roads are wide and open with lots of space to reach high speeds.
[*] The island also comes with a bunch of new challenges ruled by our three new monarchs: The Turbo Knight, Nitro Princess and the Tarmac Tyrant. As you probably guessed because of the name of the Nitro Princess, we added some new building blocks as well: Correct, we added super chargers and a brand new V-engine!
[*] The super charger consists of two building blocks, the base and the extension. You can attach the supercharger base to the PW-Blaze engine, or to the new V-engine. Then you can attach the supercharger extension to the base, to increase the power gain even more.
[*] The V-engine weighs a lot due to the size and its two cylinders. It has a lower RPM range than the other combustion engines, but a lot of power in return.
[*] On Rennpisten Insel there is also a new gems system. Instead of having to beat bronze in every race to challenge a monarch, you now have to collect a certain amount of gems.[/list]


[h3][b]Gauge Blocks[/b][/h3]
We added small attachment blocks for the driver seat. You can use those to customize the UI elements while driving. By placing gauge blocks onto the attachment block, you can determine which gauges you want to have displayed and where.

[list][*] [u][b]Speed Gauge[/b][/u]
This is the normal speed gauge. It shows RPM, the current gear and speed.
[*] [u][b]Power Curve Gauge[/b][/u]
This gauge is also not new, but you can place it now wherever you want. It displays the current power curve of your powertrain.
[*] [u][b]Car Status Gauge[/b][/u]
This gauge was also already in the game. It shows your current weight, how much damage your car has taken and whether you’re missing some wheels or downforce.
[*] [u][b]Gyro Gauge[/b][/u]
This gauge is new. It shows the current lateral and longitudinal forces on your car. It also shows the maximum forces that affected the car since you last repaired it. This could be used to evaluate your cars’ performance in terms of acceleration, brake speed and how fast you can go around corners.[/list]


[h3][b]New Building Blocks[/b][/h3]
[list][*] V-Engine: A strong and heavy combustion engine with a low RPM range.
[*] Supercharger Base: A supercharger base to slot onto the PW-Blaze or the V-engine. It increases the power in low RPM ranges.
[*] Supercharger Extension: Looks damn cool, and also increases the power in low RPM ranges even more.
[*] Smoll Suspension: An extremely small and compact suspension. In comparison to all other suspension, it doesn’t have a hole for axles, so it can just be used as a wheel to steer and roll.
[*] Keybindings Panel: A small panel you can attach anywhere to your vehicle. Then you can configure it and describe all the keybindings of your vehicle. This will then be displayed while driving if you press F1 to open the controls hints. This helps with vehicles having many or complicated keybindings.
[*] Star Connector: Similar to the ??? connector, but with four pins sticking out.
[*] Gauges and Seat Extension: We added four gauges and a seat extension block where you can attach them to your seat.
[*] 3-states Piston: We added a piston having three states. This piston starts in a half extended state, and can be contracted with one key, and extended with another one.[/list]


[h3][b]Minor Changes[/b][/h3]
[list][*] We improved challenge loading times. The big loading time came from loading the ghosts (Bronze, silver, gold and personal bests). This should happen much faster now.
[*] The small wooden poles of the checkpoints don’t damage or slow down the car anymore. They’re like butter now.
[*] Engine extension gadgets now contribute to the overall horse power of the vehicle.
[*] You can now assign controller axis like left/right stick or the triggers to stepper motor and piston keybindings.
[*] When hovering over the car stats with the mouse cursor, the car used to do an explosion animation. This was bugged in the last update, and should now be fixed again.
[*] The dynamic camera is now a little higher and further away from the car. This should make it easier to see the track and road ahead.
[*] Added a leaderboard button to the career tab, where you can inspect the leaderboards directly in the menu.
[*] A couple of months ago we updated the whole damage system of the game. We reverted the changes, where light weight parts took significantly more damage. Now battle bots should be possible again.
[*] You can now look around when sitting in first person in your seat. You can also use the scroll wheel to adjust your eye height.
[*] You can now unsubscribe from Workshop vehicles by right clicking them in your garage. So you don’t have to search for it in the workshop tab.[/list]


[h3][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/h3]
[list][*] Fixed the effect turbos and capacitors have on engines. Their added power curve is now scaled correctly, so they can be used properly with all types of engines now.
[*] Fixed that the “Loading” circle of challenges did not disappear, although the challenge was successfully loaded.
[*] Three cage parts weren’t configured to be unlocked in the ranklist career. This should be fixed now.
[*] I tried to fix the PS5 controller. You can now switch to PS5 controller input mapping in the controls settings. After that, the mapping will be changed and hopefully matches the PS5 controller properly.
[*] Fixed the leaderboards again.
[*] There was a problem with some cars, where their brakes would not work. That’s due to the ABS system I coded. I tried to adjust it, so it doesn’t prevent those cars from braking at all.
[*] Fixed a problem with the center of mass calculation. When repairing, the game sometimes recalculated the center of mass wrongly. This should now be fixed.
[*] When lowering the texture quality in graphic settings, the UI texture resolution got also reduced. Now most of the UI should be unaffected when reducing the overall texture resolution.[/list]


[h3][b]Physics Changes[/b][/h3]
[list][*] It wasn’t possible before to build an engine, which goes directly to a planetary gear and then powered a hinge joint. This should now work properly.
[*] The game now correctly calculates the rotation direction of gears and axles for everything that powers hinge joints. The game still doesn’t care about the rotation direction in the powertrain for wheels. But for everything else, you can now determine the rotation direction with the gearing. (There is a bug tho with worm gears still)
[*] We completely changed the forces and speed of hinge joints. Before, no matter which engine used, hinge joints sped up to insane speed almost instantly. Now the game actually uses the power curve of the attached engine and powertrain to determine the power and top speed of hinge joints. This means, that you can now use multiple engines and/or gearing to power hinge joints with the speed and power you want or need. This also means that hinge joints in general are now much weaker and slower. If you want to spin something heavy, it will probably take some time to accelerate to speed. Likewise if you try to spin something that doesn’t weigh much, it will spin up much faster. Hopefully this makes the whole game much more realistic and makes it much more fun to play around with hinges, since their physics and forces now also use the same forces that are used to power the wheels of cars.
[*] We changed the downforce physics. The wings now use a much more realistic force calculation. In general, they now produce less downforce than before, which should result in more realistic behavior. Due to those changes, we will reset all leaderboards of the game, so you can freshly start to conquer them.[/list]


Drive and fly safe, friends!
Marc and Simon / Creactstudios

notes.title: Show and Tell #2 - '50s-Style Bus by CatBurger23
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/f591718cc815855aca7e302bdf3cbb2877550811.jpg[/img]
[b][u]How long have you been playing Screw Drivers?[/u][/b]
I installed Screw Drivers on June 25th of 2024 and I've spent over 800 hours in game by now. I added the supporter pack soon after installing the game and recently bought the first DLC.

[b][u]How did you find out about the game, and what made you decide to play the game?[/u][/b]
I saw Scrapman playing SD on YouTube and was attracted to the game right away. During my childhood, I played a lot with LEGOs, especially LEGO Technic. I've been looking for a game which allows me to build stuff in an equal way for quite some time now, but never was able to find what I was looking for. So when I learned about SD, obviously I had to try it right away!

[b][u]What can you tell us about your vehicle?[/u][/b]
Oh, my bus?! Yeah, it's a beauty, isn't it? 😄

I took inspiration from a Saurer 2SC, a beautiful old excursion bus from the '50s. It's not an exact copy, though.

It is quite hard to realize this specific design style in SD. You know, those old cars/buses have a lot of elegantly curved shapes and replicating them is quite a challenge. Somehow, I feel especially attracted to building stuff like this. (I did something similar with my GMC '40s military trucks and the DC-3 Airliner, for example). Getting close enough to the original shapes, so that the model becomes recognizable, gives me a great sense of achievement. 🙂

Concerning the '50s bus, the new DLC parts, specifically the curved cage parts, came in very handy. (Although they are very heavy, unfortunately). First of all, to make the round shapes of the rear roof part, but also to imitate some of the numerous chrome parts and trimmings busses from this era have.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/a7b7ab01b8e1f2bc447b915d2d0431d7625c07d5.jpg[/img]
I also added a nice interior, with a lot of seats, a steering wheel and even a stick shifter. I feel like a themed build just isn't complete without interior. Especially, if you can easily look inside, as in the case of my bus. The door can be opened and I really like the little stairs at the entrance.
As a final touch, I added some interior lighting. With the new lamp parts, I just couldn't resist making this little detail.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/21d5d69805b7d50bf5ccd7cb9e7e2ff4525bbf1f.jpg[/img]
Technically, it was quite hard to make it work somewhat decently. It's a very heavy build at 5.1 tons. That causes some issues with the game physics, so the wheels tend to burn out all the time. Reducing the wind resistance and building a motor that has enough, but not too much power, brought the wheel spin down to an acceptable level. There's still a lot of wheel spin, but it settles down when reaching a certain speed. This little imperfection makes the bus less realistic, but actually very fun to drive!!! You can easily drift this 5-ton-monster through turns in a very controllable way!
So, what started out being a problem, ended up being a super fun feature and I love doing races with the bus! Even though it's far from being competitve 😄

[b][u]How did you come up with the name of the vehicle?[/u] [/b]
The name I chose isn't very creative. It just describes the build: '50s-Style Bus (Loves to drift!!!) And that's exactly what you get.

[b][u]How long did it take to create it, and do you know how many pieces there are?[/u][/b]
The bus consists of exactly 1608 parts and I worked on it for three days. Most of it was done after the first day, though. During the following days, I just added some details, like the door and the interior lighting, and optimized some things, especially the performance. All in all it took me maybe around 10-12 hours.

[b][u]Did you create it for a specific challenge, or why did you decide to create it?[/u][/b]
I didn't do a big project for quite a while, so it was about time to build something epic again. I had the idea of making a bus while building the DC3's interior. Making a bus with complete interior, too, just seemed obvious to me.

[b][u]If you could choose and new feature to add to the game, what would it be?[/u][/b]
Well, first of all there's several bugs I'd love to see being fixed and some other things which should be optimized. The functionality the game currently offers is great. In my opinion, making it all work smoothly would benefit the game more, than introducing new features and most likely new bugs in the process.

Still, since I'm very much into building and flying planes, I'd very much appreciate it, if dedicated plane parts would be introduced to the game. I designed a set of such parts for this specific purpose in Blender and provided the developers with them already. So I have high hopes, that this might become a part of the game at some point.

[img]https://media0.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExdzFtMG5rYTltNGE0eHd5YjJ3OXE3cXpsb2x2dWczbXU1NDZ2bnlqdCZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/8NR4AN1BFjR9j90hcS/giphy.gif[/img]

[b][u]Do you have any tips for a new player or someone that wants to get better at building vehicles?[/u][/b]
My advice would be to just keep building! It's like with everything in life: The more practice you get, the better the outcome will be!

For people who wanna do themed builds, I suggest trying to get the shapes right first, and worry about the technical aspects, like engines and transmissions, later!

Also, whatever you wanna build, check the workshop for something similar, download the build and analyze it in the building editor. You can learn about many building techniques this way.
And, last but not least, join the Discord! It's definitely the best resource for any kind of information or help you might need! And the community is very friendly and welcoming!

[b][u]Do you have any favorite vehicle from the Workshop that you use or take inspiration from?[/u][/b]
There's a lot of interesting things on the workshop. Flame's Ornithopters for example are amazing. Afaik, he was the first to pull it off and I highly respect his innovative talent!
The Thrust SSC made by Vidden (on the workshop his name is Skalhamn) is just crazy. Snarf's Tiger tank is stunning. Whitedwarf's propeller cars are on another level. I love Funky Friz's bulldozer. There's so many...

I wouldn't exactly say that I'm inspired by these builds, though. I take my inspiration mainly from real life models.

I'd like to say thank you to the devs for making this wonderfull, creative game. It's great how close they are to the community and how they always try to listen to what the community wants and needs! Keep up the great work!!!

Thank you for having me and giving me the chance to show off my bus!

[b]xoxo CatBurger23[/b]

Steam Workshop: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3399614123]'50s Style Bus[/url]

[u][b]Developer Comments[/b][/u]
I soo much love themed builds like this, and especially big ones like this bus. When I started creating Screw Drivers, I always imagined it to be possible to build really big vehicles, where the engine isn't even visible since it's hidden somewhere inside the car, and that the vehicle has mechanics to open/close doors etc. Hence I so much appreciate this bus from CatBurger and I love that it even drives this smoothely. Can't wait for a bus racing event! 😄 - Simon 

A Bus??? That's insane! I love all the details like the bus drivers seat with the steering wheel, the ground which instantly gives me a back to school feeling and the stairs to get into the bus.
With the sunshine of the images I wish I could be on Isola Tornanti and just drive around in the bus to all the sightseeing points of the island. 
And the bus driver is an grumpy king whos condemned to drive all the Prince and Princess around.
Love it! - Mark

notes.title: 🔥 Get your Engine roaring with the Performance+ Update V0.4.1.12!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/86d2da349ca28627b12fd57e731a83e0e71654b5.png[/img]

Greetings, Drivers!

Even though it's almost February: We wish you all a happy, healthy and successful year 2025!

And we are starting the new year with update v0.4.1.1.2, or as we call it: The [b]Performance+ Update[/b]! We took the whoooooole projekt and lifted it onto the new Unity version to clean up the project and boost the Performance of the game. So this update is mostly about optimizing the game so you can either now play the game without crashing and crying or play it 3 times on the same device. Depending on your setup!

So here is a list with all the stuff that changed besides the better FPS with this new Performance plus update:

[b]BETTER PERFORMANCE[/b]
[list][*] We improved and optimized the game overall, so memory usage, cpu and graphics usage should all improve with this

notes.title: 🐍 Screw Drivers supports Razer's Sensa HD Haptics and Chroma peripherals!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/f88a829ffa2613ba5536bf4fee47a55c56e5d5f2.jpg[/img]

Greetings all!
 
If you've been playing or following [b]Screw Drivers[/b] for a while (since around mid-September or earlier), you may have noticed that we announced [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1279510/view/4677641107692320262]at the time[/url] that the game would be one of the early bird titles to support Razer's [b]Sensa HD Haptics[/b] peripherals. You know, that gaming cushion that attaches to your chair and can literally kick your butt.
 
[b]And yes, we kept our word: Screw Drivers supports Sensa HD Haptics peripherals and the Chroma RGB ecosystem from TODAY with the update V0.3.15.9![/b]
 
But let's start from the beginning, with two questions: [i]'Why are you doing this?'[/i] and [i]'How should a cushion for my chair improve my gaming experience?'[/i]. Let's answer the first question first: The reason is me, Tim. Hi! Well, personally I am very open-minded about such technical gadgets. And I am convinced that an intensive gaming experience can benefit from being more than just an audiovisual experience. I am a big fan of strengthening the immersion of video games to delve even deeper and making it possible to experience them with as many senses as possible.
 
That's exactly why I'm the one here at Headup who initiates such implementations. So, I asked myself which of our games could benefit most from also being a 'tangible' experience (which is also the answer to the second question).
 
And a 'sandboxy car crafting and racing game' sounded like a really good fit. After all, in [b]Screw Drivers[/b] you can not only assemble your own vehicles physically correctly in the editor, but also drive them and disassemble them back into their individual parts. Jackpot! And all these actions and movements ended up being accompanied and reinforced by haptic feedback.
 
The gaming cushion ([url=https://www.razer.com/gaming-chairs-accessories/razer-freyja]Razer Freyja[/url]) has six haptic zones: two in the shoulder blade area, two in the lower back area; one each on the left and on the right. Plus one zone under each bun. The haptic feedback can be controlled in terms of intensity and therefore be adapted to different use cases. And with the mixture of a racing game and haptic feedback, most of you will probably think of crashes in no time. And yes, that's exactly what we have implemented haptically, of course; in the three different levels: 'Low', 'Medium' and 'Strong'.

Depending on how intense your crash is, the cushion will let you feel it!

But the combination of [b]Screw Drivers[/b] and the cushion gave even more interesting scope! Due to the tires of a vehicle on the left and right side, and the haptic zones on the left and right side of the cushion, you can feel different ground coverings through different haptic feedback: asphalt, grass, gravel, sand and water cause different feedback; also in the 'Low', 'Medium' and 'Strong' levels. So if you drive your vehicle on asphalt on the left and sand on the right, you will feel it through your back and bottom.

But crashes and ground coverings are only two of the examples that could be implemented in [b]Screw Drivers[/b] in a very cool 'tangible' way. In addition, different engine RPMs are implemented with different levels of haptic feedback, as well as gear changes and drifts. Furthermore various actions that are necessary in the editor when building a vehicle. 
 
As I said, I am a friend of gimmicks that increase immersion. That's why I also love it when the gameplay is extended beyond the limits of the screen through RGB illumination. And that is the reason why the haptic effects are additionally supported by RGB effects in Razer's Chroma ecosystem. An intensive crash is not only kicking your butt, it will also be communicated through the Chroma peripherals!
 
Well, in the end I can only speak for us (Creactstudios and Headup) and myself personally, and we are really happy with the results of both Sensa HD Haptics and [b]Chroma[/b] and how it supports and accompanies the [b]Screw Drivers[/b] experience, immersion, and the fun.

Personally, I love it. ❤️ If I didn't already have it, the cushion would definitely be on top of my Christmas wish list. 🎄

Pre-seasonal greetings!
Tim

notes.title: 🔥 The Stunt Showdown DLC is OUT NOW; plus Update V0.3.15.9 released!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/d973a423e7e9ed04b03082d4bd68ed45bedb9810.png[/img]

Happy DLC Launch Tuesday everybody!

This might become our longest update posting so far, and the reason for that might be that we’re releasing our very first DLC, the [u][b]Stunt Showdown[/b][/u]! If you want to support us and [b]Screw Drivers[/b] further, you can now get the Stunt Showdown DLC and unlock Isola Tartaruga, a new volcano with lots of stunt challenges and new building blocks to pimp up your cars and impress the crowds with your jumps, tricks and style!

Check it out, and thank you for all your support throughout our development. We appreciate all of you playing and enjoying our game, and joining us on this crazy adventure. We’re always eager to hear what you think, so feel free to reach out to us on discord, here on Steam or through the feedback form in the main menu. We’re looking forward to hearing from you:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3288110/Screw_Drivers__Stunt_Showdown/



We've also released a new update to Screw Drivers that brings the game to V0.3.15.9. Among other things, it adds custom input mappings, spring loaded shifters and new building parts, and much more!

[h3][b]Full Changelog of V0.3.15.9:[/b][/h3]

[u][b]Custom Input Mappings[/b][/u]
You can now change and define your own inputs to most driving and building actions. This allows you to rebind the air control both on controller and keyboard. You can also change the bindings for gear shifting, which allows you to use manual gear shifts on controller as well.

And this now also allows for the usage of most steering wheels. I only tested it with my old G25 steering wheel, but the game should detect all kinds of input axles, so hopefully most devices will work. You can also enable or disable the steering angle limit at high speeds, which is useful when driving with keyboard, but when using a controller or steering wheel, it might feel more natural to turn that off.


[u][b]Spring Loaded Shifters[/b][/u]
[list][*] We changed the shifting times of gear shifters in general. Before, the time it took to shift gears up and down was constant at around 150ms. Now, the game calculated all the weight attached to the tip of a gear shifter. The heavier the mechanical assembly attached to the gear shifter is, the slower it will shift gears using that gear shifter. So if you want to reduce the shift times, you have to reduce the weight attached to the tip of the shifter as much as possible by using short axles and few and small gears.
[*] We also introduce two new building parts: The spring loaded shifters. They work exactly like the normal gear shifters, but compared to the normal ones, these have a difference in shifting times when contracting or extending the shifter. Due to the spring, moving the tip of the shifter to the outside is extremely fast, while contracting the spring and moving the tip to the inside of the shifter takes slightly more time. On average, the spring loaded shifters have faster shift times than the normal shifters. And their shift times also depend on the attached weight.
[*] Shift times of normal shifters: Between 100ms and 300ms
[*] Shift times of spring loaded shifters (Moving tip outwards): Between 20ms and 80ms
[*] Shift times of spring loaded shifters (Moving tip inwards): Between 150ms and 350ms[/list]


[u][b]New Building Parts[/b][/u]
[list][*] Exhaust: The exhaust is only decorative. It produces some light, environmental friendly smoke when accelerating. When when shifting gears, it sometimes spits a little bit of fire.
[*] Headlight and brake light: We added two light parts to the game. The headlights, which you can switch on and off with an assigned key. And the brake lights, which light up when you’re braking.
[*] Seat: You can now attach a Driving Seat to your car to access first person driving. The camera will then be a little above the seats position. For now only the Seat will be dropped but soon we will add some nice module expansions for the Seat![/list]


[u][b]Wheels now have Camber[/b][/u]
[list][*] We added camber to the wheels in the game. Here we made the following changes to the dirt and the street suspensions:
[*] Street suspensions: If you enable the advanced building mode in the general settings menu, you can now configure camber for the street suspensions. This allows you to possibly increase grip in fast driven corners.
[*] Dirt suspensions: Since dirt suspensions were essentially better in all aspects compared to the street suspensions, we introduced a “natural” camber for the dirt suspensions. They now tilt the wheel when the spring is being compressed or relaxed. This should slightly worsen the general grip and handling of dirt suspensions, since the wheels aren’t planted flat to the surface all the time anymore. Our goal is to make them look funny because of the camber, but also to create a difference between street and dirt suspensions, so both have a field of application for different kinds of vehicle types.[/list]


[u][b]Minor Changes[/b][/u]
[list][*] When calculating a vehicle in the building editor and closing the analysis window, unconnected parts of the vehicle will fly away for a couple of seconds, so you can see which parts of the vehicle are not connected to the rest of the vehicle.
[*] We updated the leaderboards graphic to show the player names and actual times of players around yourself.
[*] We added two new optional challenges to Isola tornanti.
[*] When calculating the strength and stiffness of suspensions, the game now looks at the weight of the attached rigidbody individually, instead of considering the total weight of a vehicle.
[*] To prevent abuse of the car classes system, the game now only considers the weight of the lightest rigidbody for the car classes, instead of using the total weight. (Catapult class is planned but we haven’t gotten to implement it yet)
[*] Moved all the ghost races data of bronze, silver and gold times to a separate folder, so it’s not loaded into the RAM when not needed.
[*] We updated the weights of all gears and axles. They are now much lighter than before, allowing for bigger and more complex gear transmissions without impacting the weight of the vehicle too much.
[*] Reworked the glass material
[/list]


[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]
[list][*] Fixed and polished terrain on Isola tornanti
[*] Added outside map catcher to Isola tornanti to prevent cars from falling through the ground and not respawning.
[*] Optional challenges weren’t playable in creative mode, if you only play the tech tree career. Now they also appear, if you beat the Secret Queen in the tech tree career.[/list]


Drive safe, friends!
Marc and Simon / Creactstudios

Dear Screw Drivers Community, 

Allow me to briefly introduce myself: Dieter here, CEO and founder of Headup. I rarely get involved with communications, so reaching out to you, the players, is somewhat new to me - hoping to strike the right tone. 😊

The reason I’m writing today is to share some happy news and give you some insight into our - well, actually, your - numbers for the game. I know it’s not common practice to do this, but I feel it might be interesting for some of you. 

First, I’m thrilled to share that [b]Screw Drivers[/b] has hit an outstanding milestone this week, thanks to all of you. The game has shattered expectations, with over half a million (yes, 500,000+) Steam users claiming it, leaving us absolutely speechless. 


[b]Here’s a breakdown of some key numbers as of this moment:[/b] 
[list][*] 500,000 free licenses claimed (meaning players have added it to their library) 
[*] Over 315,000 unique users have played the game so far 
[*] It currently has an 87% positive user rating from about 2,500 reviews 
[*] And what makes us most proud: The community has created and shared almost 13,000 (!) Workshop items for the game, ranging from cars and planes to really unique machinery. This is what we always dreamed of when we started the project - giving you the tools and watching the players go wild and create amazing things![/list]

On behalf of both the studio and the publishing team, I want to express our deepest gratitude for joining us on this journey and dedicating your time and love to the game. We know you have countless other entertainment options competing for your time, so believe me when I say how much we appreciate the time you’ve spent with us. 

On the flip side, I’d also like to share some information about the game’s financials. So far, we’ve prefunded all development and marketing efforts, by offering only a supporter pack. To be transparent, about 3,000 players have supported us with a purchase, translating to roughly 1% of all players (or 0.6% of all licenses claimed). While we’re incredibly thankful for every supporter (sending our biggest hugs), as you can see, this is not a sustainable level of income to support ongoing development in the long term. We consciously chose this route in the beginning, and the numbers and feedback have validated the relevance of the game to you and to us. 

Our vision is to establish [b]Screw Drivers[/b] as a growing and free sandbox for all engineers, drivers, and creators in the future. We don’t want to rely on FOMO-driven purchases or artificial paywalls. What I’m trying to say is: We’re on a quest to find the fairest and most honest free-to-play monetization model that will allow the game’s development to thrive without taking away the fun or opportunities from the community. 

So what’s the plan? We will keep the game free. Period. Quality-of-life improvements, bug fixes, more localizations, game modes, you name it. Instead of creating barriers, we want to offer more sophisticated experiences to players who want to dive deeper. While I can’t (and don’t want to 😊) reveal the exact roadmap yet, we’ll be introducing theme-based DLC packs at reasonable prices, allowing for the creation of more advanced or themed vehicles. This way, you will still be able to enjoy the game for free, but there will be an optional, additional layer for the most dedicated creators. 

We’re committed to being as transparent, honest, and approachable as possible and look forward to continuing this journey with our most valuable asset - you, the players, and the time you invest in the game! 

Sincerely, 
Dieter 
CEO/Founder, Headup

notes.title: The "Damage Model and Car Classes" Update for Screw Drivers is live!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/3b4bcb211bd2b35a1aa43dc91c64b6577b48e6e3.png[/img]

Happy Thursday, friends!

And what a Thursday it is! Just in case you didn't know yet: it's (the highly official) [b]“Damage Model and Car Classes” Thursday[/b] today. And we're celebrating this with a new update for [b]Screw Drivers[/b]!

Namely with the update V0.3.13.1, which is also called the “Damage Model and Car Classes” Update. for this we completely updated the damage model, and added a new UI to visualize the health of the vehicle. There are now also 37 new car classes, you can drive against the ghost of your personal best, and much more.

See for yourself:

[h3][b][u]Full changelog of v0.3.10.12[/u][/b][/h3]


[u][b]Damage Model[/b][/u]

We completely updated the damage model, and at the same time we added a new UI to visualize the health of the vehicle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/c3eebb6f47efcc851f7f3d8d286d503c1ca777d5.jpg[/img]
[b]There are five things which changed in the way vehicles take damage:[/b]
[list][*] Before, the amount of damage taken increased when the vehicle was heavier. So a vehicle weighing 1000kg did take double the amount of damage when crashing compared to a 500kg vehicle. This is now changed, so the weight of the own vehicle doesn’t affect the amount of damage taken.
[*] Before, the amount of damage taken was linear to the velocity when crashing. Now, the amount of damage scales with the square of the velocity when crashing. This means, at lower speeds you will now take less damage than before, and when crashing with higher speeds vehicles now take more damage.
[*] Before, the damage has been propagated through the vehicle evenly. Now the damage is propagated more towards the upper parts of a vehicle, and a little less to the parts at the bottom. This is not realistic, but it helps to protect the wheels of vehicles. It also means, that you can how build some chassis construction towards the top of your vehicle to make it more resistant against crashes.
[*] If you lose engines your car will also lose power. The powertrain is not recalculated to correctly adjust the power curve, but depending on  the power of the broken engine, your vehicle will lose an according percentage of total power. You can also see this in the new damage UI whenever an engine breaks apart.
[*] If you lose mechanical building blocks like gears, axles, wheels or engines, your top speed will be reduced slightly. You can also see this in the new damage UI as soon as you lose some mechanical building blocks.[/list]
On top of the top speed and power reduction, you can now also see the amount of downforce your vehicle has, and the amount of wheels that are still intact. And in the middle you can see the total damage your vehicle has taken.



[u][b]New car classes[/b][/u]

We completely overdid it, and we replaced the old car classes ranging from F to S+ with 37 new car classes. The old car classes tried to estimate, how fast a car is overall. Since that’s insanely difficult and didn’t work out that well, we now created the new car classes which categorize all vehicles according to three aspects:
[list][*] Acceleration
[*] Downforce
[*] Weight and Tip-Over[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/23f25ee7c7cc6ef645055ae360a66ca3fc7b0eab.jpg[/img]
This separates all vehicles according to these three stats. There are four areas of accelerations, three areas of downforce and three differentiating vehicles by their weight and tip-over value. This makes 36 car classes. And to get to 37, we created a new car class specifically for propeller vehicles. So if your vehicle has any downforce and it has a rotatable hinge joint, it will be considered a propeller vehicle. This should help to differentiate prop cars from other cars and gives them a special leaderboard.

We will let you play around with the car classes yourself, and let us know what you think!



[u][b]Drive against the ghost of your personal best[/b][/u]

That’s right, the game now stores your personal best laps for each challenge. When you drive a challenge a second time, you can enable and disable the ghosts you wanna drive against. These are the bronze, silver and gold medals as well as your personal best and your personal best in your current car class.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/cb08a3528622fc0ad931f9756cac60b3abc06722.jpg[/img]


[u][b]Major Changes[/b][/u]
[list][*] We added a lot of big signs to most challenges. They should help to make it more visible and more clear where the track is going and where sharp curves are ahead.
[*] New calculation of acceleration statistic (again). Now the game only looks at the power curve between 0 and 100 km/h and calculates a weighted area of the curve. This weighted area makes acceleration in lower speeds more important than acceleration values of higher speeds close to 100km/h.
[*] Added new optional challenge: Pepper Sprint[/list]


[u][b]Minor Changes[/b][/u]
[list][*] Added two entries to the general settings, where you can invert the mouse movement for the camera in driving mode.
[*] When you try to add a creative mode car or a workshop vehicle to your garage in career, the game now shows you how much money you are missing, in case you don’t have enough money to buy all the missing parts right now.
[*] We reduced the details resolution of the terrain, which reduces the amount of polygons being rendered.[/list]


[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]
[list][*] Fixed a bug which allowed you to instantly teleport to the finish line in acceleration challenges or in A-to-B challenges.
[*] Fixed tech tree unlock condition of the worm gear. Now it can be unlocked on the Double 8 challenge or the Rock and Drift challenge.
[*] The center of mass indicator isn’t tilted anymore.
[*] In the combustion engine tutorial, the red outline wasn’t showing to indicate the removal of the small electric engine. This should now be fixed.
[*] Fixed a bug where the center of mass of all rigidbodies was calculated wrongly when repairing the vehicle.
[*] When pressing the 'X' button on the controller in the building editor, the context menu of the garage opened and closed without being visible. This is now fixed.
[*] Fixed the calculation of the tip-over value, which sometimes was higher than it actually is when using multiple rigidbodies in one vehicle.
[*] Fixed a bug where the turbo and the big combustion engine weren’t unlockable anymore in the giant bridge challenge, since I screwed up something there accidentally. Should work again now.
[*] We fixed the destructable objects which weren’t working correctly: Barrel, small fence and the lantern.[/list]

Drive safe, friends!

notes.title: Screw Drivers - Show and Tell #1: Fancy Plane 2.1
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/144abb6ddd9d13dfc22a83ec3b7e051af74d1622.jpg[/img]
Greetings everyone, 

Every day, we see new, unique creations shared in the Steam Workshop, and we are always stunned by how creative people can be. In Show and Tell, we are taking a deeper look at some of the great creations and the people behind those creations!

In this first episode of Show and Tell, we are looking at a vehicle that is not about being on the road but more to be in the sky. How is that possible? We don’t know, but let’s see what Spectre, the creator of ‘Fancy Plane’ has to say.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/198fb365814e565210a648c68497f38c7eff1722.jpg[/img]

[b]How long have you been playing Screw Drivers?[/b]
At the time of writing, I had a combined total of around 200 hours in the game, but at the time of creating Fancy Plane 1.0, I had only 18 hours. 

[b]How did you find out about the game, and what made you decide to play the game?[/b]
I saw Scrapman's first video on the Screw Drivers Demo and got so inspired I stopped watching halfway through to play the game. 

[b]What can you tell us about your vehicle?[/b]
I know it is among the first flying machines created in this game (1.0). I've been working hard on improving flight stability and multiplayer support. Otherwise, it is just a very simple plane. I know there are better ones out there, but I'm proud of being one of the first to introduce propellers to the masses. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/837d7f49672d298cfa8bca4beed551338c49426c.jpg[/img]
[b]How did you come up with the name of the vehicle?[/b]
I've never been good at naming things. I just named it what it was; I think it looks fancy :D 

[b]How long did it take to create it, and do you know how many pieces there are?[/b]
It's been a couple of months since I originally built the first version, but I remember it took about 3 hours. Version 2.1 states it has 303 parts.

[b]Did you create it for a specific challenge, or why did you decide to create it?[/b]
I only built it to see if I could. Prior to building it, I had not seen any flying machines in screwdrivers; I wasn't even on Discord. I figured the spoiler parts were simple enough to create a propeller with, and I was right! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/c6ace4b90f820888b4a3be126c34c62a2efb1e77.jpg[/img]
[b]If you could choose a new feature to add to the game, what would it be?[/b]
Stunts. Those were fun in the demo to get loads of money.  

[b]Do you have any tips for a new player or someone who wants to get better at building vehicles?[/b]
Other people's creations can be a huge learning experience. Don't forget that you can duplicate other people’s creations and tear them apart in the editor to see how they work. 

[b]Do you have any favorite vehicle from the Workshop that you use or take inspiration from?[/b]
Of course, the "Bluey-7 Helicopter" by Operator Snow. He personally showed me how to add a custom thumbnail to my creation (His helicopter was the first ever to have one), and I don't think my plane would be the 10th most subscribed vehicle in the workshop without him.

[b]Comments from the Developers:[/b]
[i]“I am impressed with how you figured out how to build a propeller system yourself without even looking at other flying vehicles. Even if we did not yet implement anything supporting such flying machines, the player of Screw Drivers is getting more and more expert in building better and better airplanes and other crazy stuff. I think we are both really looking forward diving into the topic of airplanes in Screw Drivers ourselves.”[/i] - Marc/Tudl

[i]“I love how you just went ahead and tried to build a propeller powered plane without knowing if it's possible. That's pretty much how I like to approach building stuff on my own as well when trying something new. And I think this is where creations are made, that exceed what the game was meant to be and which also inspire me as a developer about what is currently possible in the game, and what we might add to the game in the future as well.”[/i] - Simon/SapphireHD6970


[b]Do you want to try out the plane? Subscribe to it in the Steam Workshop![/b]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3271890982]Fancy Plane 2.1[/url]

notes.title: Quality of Life Update V0.3.12.1 adds Editor Improvements, Building Blocks, ...
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/c9853d36ea8747727f981cfcc68f3f7a8e6ea568.png[/img]

Welcome to our second Early Access milestone update!

Since the last [b]Screw Drivers[/b] update, there was gamescom, some vacation and some flue. But still, we’ve prepared a massive update for you, with some awesome quality of life changes to the building editor. This update was originally planned as the fifth milestone update on our Early Access roadmap, but as QoL improvements were requested by you more often, we have prioritised the update.

As a result, the ‘Character Editor’ update, originally planned as the second update, has been swapped with the ‘Quality of Life’ update and is now the fifth on the roadmap. The roadmap on the product page has been updated and adapted accordingly.

We also added three new gears to play around with, some other building blocks, new challenges, a new leaderboard and much more. We also implemented a peer-to-peer multiplayer system, which should allow you to host your own server without forwarding ports in the router. Feel free to try that out as well.

And we also added a vote to the main menu, whether you would prefer the ranklist career or the tech tree career as main career mode for the future. Let us know which one you enjoyed the most!

So here is the full changelog of [b]V0.3.12.1[/b]. And as always, please share your thoughts & feedback with us!


[h3][u][b]BUILDING EDITOR[/b][/u][/h3]

[b]Mutli Selection Mode[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/890353a3ece52dd57a329705bceaef96e5a9eef5.png[/img]
You are now able to multi select multiple parts of your car and move them around using the arrow keys and the scroll wheel. It’s also possible now to delete, colorize, rotate and copy a selection of parts. To select multiple parts just hold SHIFT and click multiple parts hold down the left mouse button and drag a selection square over your screen.

Then use the arrow keys and the scroll wheel to move the selection around. Or use the little action buttons to color the whole selection, rotate it or duplicate it.


[b]Mirror Mode[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/6a12fb4c3039d8c658f8a844ed2e269c26ad5214.png[/img]
We added a mirror mode to the building editor. You can activate it by pressing 'M', then move the mirror-plane left and right with the arrow keys. And all the blocks you place or remove on one side will be mirrored on the other side.


[b]Hot bar[/b]
The building editor now has a hot bar. You can assign up to 9 blocks to the numeric keys of your keyboard to quickly access your favorite parts. When you open the parts menu, hover a part and press the alpha key to assign that part to that slot.


[b]Color palette[/b]
You can now select colors by opening a color palette on the bottom of the screen. There you can see and select all available and unlocked colors. You can still switch between colors quickly by using the scroll wheel.


[h3][u][b]NEW BUILDING BLOCKS[/b][/u][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/7a81fd1028827645ad54da22b3bcbdad86185ef1.png[/img]
[list][*] [b]Worm Gear:[/b] A small typical worm gear. It can be used to create extreme gear ratios. Logically it has two gear teeth.
[*] [b]Plate Gear:[/b] A flat plate of the size of the medium gear, but the teeth are angled in a 90 degree angle. With this you can both implement a gear transmission, but also transmit power around the corner.
[*] [b]Small Corner Gear: [/b]Works pretty similar to the current corner gear to transmit power around the corner. But this is much smaller, so it uses less space. And it can not be used to transmit power sideways.
[*] [b]Large Shark Fin:[/b] A bigger shark fin with a bigger area and thus bigger force in the wind.
[*] [b]1x1 building block:[/b] Like a beam, but only one hole in length.
[*] [b]2x2 building block:[/b] Like two beams x2 on top of each other and glued together.
[*] [b]Axle x10:[/b] A 10 blocks long powertrain axle.[/list]


[h3][u][b]MAJOR CHANGES[/b][/u][/h3]


[b]New Challenges[/b]
There are two new Optional Challenges on the Main Island and three new Challenges on the Supersonic Racetrack including a slightly new kind of challenge type


[b]A Brand new Leaderboard[/b]
We switched the old and bugged leaderboard with a new one holding way more useful information. You are now categorized in a new way showing you in which percentage of the players your driven time is. You can still see your global rank, but now it matters, if you’re in the top 5%, top 20% or top 50% of all players. Accordingly you’re categorized to be in the sapphire, gold, silver or bronze area.


[b]Update to wind resistance[/b]
The old wind resistance calculation didn’t calculate what you would expect. Since some cars with flat surfaces had less wind resistance than aerodynamically built cars. We changed the whole system, so now it should make more sense in general. You can now also see where your car suffers the most wind resistance. The wind streams with high wind resistance are colored now, and you can also see small pop ups showing the amount and position of the causes of wind resistance.


[b]Easy multiplayer hosting[/b]
We added a peer-to-peer multiplayer solution, which should allow server hosting without having to forward ports in your router. You can try this out in the main menu, by just clicking on host and see if you and your friends can connect to your server. As soon as you have connected to your own server, invite your friends through steam, and hopefully, everything works smoothly.


[h3][u][b]MINOR CHANGES[/b][/u][/h3]

[b]Take-off bridge[/b]
On Pulau Mahkota there is now a take-off bridge near the harbor for airplane like vehicles with a spawn point.


[b]New car stat[/b]
We added a new car statistic to the game: The tip-over value. This should indicate, how prone a vehicle is to tip over while cornering. It is being calculated by dividing the height of the center of mass by the maximum sideways distance of your wheels.


[h3][u][b]BUG FIXES[/b][/u][/h3]
Removed invisible colliders in A-to-B races, which sometimes catapulted cars into the air near the start or finish line.


Drive safe, friends. And have a relaxing weekend!
Marc and Simon / Creactstudios

notes.title: Major Update V0.3.11.1 adds 2 new Multiplayer Modes, Changes and Fixes!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/c5e16cd084b2baaba46e12a4a340e2996977b2ca.jpg[/img]

Happy Friday everyone!

Today, we reached our first milestone of Early Access: [b]It’s the multiplayer modes update![/b]

We added two game modes to multiplayer, the automatic races and speed building. Unfortunately, the keep the flag mode isn’t ready yet, because we started working on improving the building editor last week as well, since we think that is something important we want to add to the game earlier than planned. So you can expect some building editor improvements in the coming weeks.

Let us know what you think about the update, as always please share your thoughts and feedback with us. Of course we have even more plans for multiplayer, and there is so much more to come in the future, as well as improvements to hosting your own servers, we also haven’t forgotten about that ;D

[h3][b][u]Cheers guys, and here are the patchnotes of v0.3.11.1:[/u][/b][/h3]

[b]Multiplayer[/b]
[list][*] We created two game modes for multiplayer: Automatic races, and Speed Building
[*] In Automatic races, as the name suggests, the server will automatically start random races. Players can then participate in the races and gain points for beating the other players. After five rounds, a winner is crowned and a new cycle of five random races starts
[*] In Speed Building, the server selects a random race, and a random set of rules. Then all players have 20 minutes time to build a car that satisfies these rules to participate in the race
[*] Apart from the two new game modes, we also added the possibility to define your own set of rules. As the server host, you can define and configure custom rules for the vehicle weight, power, acceleration and so on. This way, you can create your very own rules for your server[/list]
[b]Major Changes[/b]
[list][*] We added optional challenges to the game. These are challenges which are invisible, until you beat the secret queen. Then the optional challenges will appear and can be driven to climb the leaderboards, or to be driven in multiplayer
[*] We added three fighting arenas to the Supersonic map. These can be used to play some fighting PVP in multiplayer[/list]
[b]Minor Changes[/b]
[list][*] If you restart a challenge, the loading time should be greatly reduced, because the game now caches the ghost race data of the last driven challenge
[*] You can now color the carbon wings properly as well
[*] You can now switch back to the old camera movement in the building editor in the general settings (Instead of only being accessible through the F9 key)
[*] Engines now actually have colliders. Gears still have no colliders tho, so you don’t have to worry about them touching the ground
[*] Tech Tree can be toggled with the right stick on controller
[*] Reduced the hit box of the small dirt wheel, since it was bigger than the hit box of the wider dirt wheel. This is the hit box when building, so it should be possible to build closer to the small dirt wheel now.
[*] Added new building part: Beam x4
[*] Added two new experimental camera modes: Orbit, and free orbit
[*] Added an FPS limit of 100 to the graphics settings menu
[*] Reduced the weight of the corner gear from 6kg to 4kg
[*] We fixed the calculation of the center of mass for a lot of parts. In big combustion engines for example, the center of mass was offset to the side. This should now be fixed for most parts
[*] We further improved the performance of the game especially in multiplayer. Mainly we decreased the physics tick-rate, which has been pretty high so far.. With the new physics tick-rate, the physics behavior should not have changed by much, but at the same time the game should run more smoothly, especially with many cars in multiplayer.[/list]
[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list][*] We re-simulated all destructible objects in the game. During our heavy optimization a month ago, we made some of the destructibles behave weirdly. Now most of them should behave correctly again when driven into
[*] Fixed a potential issue, where it wasn’t possible to navigate the garage menu with controller.
[*] Renaming a car category in the garage was assigned to the ‘A’ button on controller. This has been fixed, and it is now the left stick
[*] Fixed a rare bug, which caused the garage to crash and not show any cars anymore.
[*] When making wheels steerable, they sometimes rotated upside-down instead of left-right. This should now be fixed
[*] Fixed wrongly configured weight for unlocking the deco lasercut part in the tech tree career
[*] We fixed the mini map on the Supersonic map. The map there was only a placeholder and not an actual mini map. Now it should actually represent the map properly.[/list]

Drive safe, friends. And have a relaxing weekend!
Marc and Simon / Creactstudios

notes.title: How to start a dedicated multiplayer server for Screw Drivers!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/1ed994caac6da2e052b4a39dbe1d908fcf2ac5e4.jpg[/img]

Hey all,  

In this guide, we will show you how you can set up your very own dedicated [b]Screw Drivers[/b] server to play on with your friends.  

The dedicated server program is included in the game, and when going into Multiplayer, you will find a hosting button. When you enter the hosting window, you will be greeted by instructions on which ports need to be opened in your router for the server to function.  

[u][b]Ports: [/b][/u][list]
[*] 8766 
[*] 27011 
[*] 38000 (as the default port and can be changed in the server program/settings) [/list]
*All ports need to be set up with a User Datagram Protocol (UDP) 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/64a3b1309bc3ce0be658d3cecd0c4d37a4a27e21.png[/img]

[h3][u][b]How to open ports in the router: [/b][/u][/h3]

First, you need to connect to your router software, and the most standard way to do that is to write your router's standard IP address ([b]192.168.1.1[/b]— this can vary depending on where you live and the brand of the router) into a web browser; this will take you to your router. (If you don’t know your IP address, you can look it up by searching for your internet provider or go down in this guide and read ‘[b]How to find my internal IP Address:[/b]’) 

After you log in, you need to locate a tab called WAN; the layout can vary depending on the brand of the router.  [i](The layout can look different depending on the router)[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/91d8c9717c91daa56cfbe0d3ccac70c423768841.png[/img]

You will most likely have a tab called Port Forwarding in the WAN tab. This is where we will enter the ports that the router and game need to work together.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/ddafa5fd5b7a11383a33c07fb53e65fa90cf411a.png[/img]

If port forwarding is inactive, you need to enable it; then, you need to add a new profile. [olist]
[*] Enable Port Forwarding 
[*] Add Profile[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/63d62a83edf972737b609bd5167d4f0f14b3f8f2.png[/img]
[olist]
[*] Add Service Name (This can be called anything, we called all three Screw Drivers) 
[*] Change Protocol to UDP 
[*] Add External port (8766),(27011) and (38000) 
[*] Add your internal IP address [/olist]
You need to do this 3 times, one for each external port.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/78c2a75289398e7503dc6849e13dbf3eef2a8f4b.png[/img]

[h3][u][b]How to find my internal IP Address: [/b][/u][/h3]

Press the Windows icon in the Hotbar, and write command or CMD 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/2640c4b49000dae15b74c6699168603b9363d552.png[/img]

Command Prompt will open, and here you will write ([b]ipconfig[/b]) 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/9f41a758fbbb789005afe3db62991b1cf0f43cb0.png[/img]
When you press enter a lot of data will be shown and here you will see both your internal IP address, but also the router IP address.  [olist]
[*] Internal IP Address 
[*] Router IP Address [/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/eb3163ee7ffc700e39eda348ec290f4e3bb19c99.png[/img]

Now, when you have your internal IP address, you can add that to your port and press okay. Do this for all three ports.

When you are done, you should have three ports that will forward data to your dedicated server when you start hosting.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/f923117db9b9a2cecdf8f03eaa6809ae0ecd3a70.png[/img]

Now we are done opening the ports, so the only thing left is hosting a server! 

Tab back into the Screw Drivers game to the server hosting menu. After choosing a Server name, password, and the number of players, you press Start server. You will see a window opening and begin starting up the window, and as soon as you see ‘Connected to Steam Successfully’ your server will be online for others to join.   

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/5b34fc00400fe5a0b6dd06a93b139ea816084dbb.png[/img]
When starting the server for the first time, a window will pop up, and you need to press allow access for the server to go through the Windows Firewall. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/345ce52d39ea7d417364737c6caaf91be0c58428.png[/img]

When that is done, you will automatically be connected to the server, and you will be in the garage. You can now start playing while you wait for your friends or others to join. You can also invite friends directly through your friend list as well.  

[h3][u][b]Troubleshooting [/b][/u][/h3][list]
[*] If friends cannot connect to your server, check the firewall settings and make sure, that the "Screw Drivers Server.exe" is given access through the firewall.  
[*] If you cannot see the "Connected to Steam Successfully" message, make sure that Steam is running and you are logged in. [/list]

We hope this helps. If you have any questions, please feel free to join our Discord, and we will help you set up your own server!  

Have fun, and drive safe!
Marc and Simon / Creactstudios

So, here is the very short changelog of [b]v0.2.14.10[/b]: 

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed, that the game freezes for a couple of seconds when entering the main menu.
[*] Fixed car calculation algorithm, which was faulty when placing the corner gears in some specific constellations.
[/list]
Keep on being amazed while we work full throttle on the new version, which will be available in early access soon!

Please keep the feedback coming! 

Drive Safe,
Marc and Simon / Creactstudios

notes.title: New Update - Thank you for all the feedback!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44759059/ad201740e688485ecfa1412fa070be0c38cb78db.png[/img]
Hey, fellow car crashers… er, race drivers! 

It’s been just over a week since we released the Project Vroom Vroom prototype, and we really loved seeing all the creativity you have already displayed! This is a dream project for us, and we are very keen on getting and listening to your invaluable feedback. 

Thanks a million for engaging in our game!

Since its release, we have been working hard on updates and fixes for Vroom Vroom. Below, you can find quite a long list of all the stuff we’ve already put in the game.

Please feel free to continue suggesting both changes and additions, as well as bug reporting!

[b][u][h3]Full changelog:[/h3][/u][/b]
[b]Weekly challenge[/b][list]
[*]Added the first weekly challenge to the game. You can start it from the main menu.[/list]
[b]King challenges[/b][list]
[*]New Speed King challenge: The looooop (and yes, it contains a loop)[/list]
[b]New Building Colors [/b][list]
[*]We have hidden eight new part colors somewhere on the map. They look like little books. Find them in the free drive to unlock some new colors for building your vehicles![/list]
[b]Minor changes[/b][list]
[*]The “Dirt Wheel Medium” now only weighs 30kg instead of 60kg.
[*]The current time between checkpoints of the speed king is now displayed with a drop shadow, so it should be better readable even in front of bright, blue sky.
[*]Added a Discord invitation button to the main menu.
[*]You can now enable camera orbiting mode in general settings. This allows you to freely rotate the camera around your vehicle.
[*]The red stones inside the half-pipe now have colliders.
[*]In creative mode, all king challenges can be played now. No matter what level you have.
[*]Instead of showing that unlocking creative mode takes 15 minutes, it now displays 30 minutes as average time to unlock the game mode.
[*]The wings are now colorable. Only the carbon wing is not colorable, since, well, it is made out of carbon, and it is absolutely unthinkable to put paint onto something so beautiful.
[*]You can now switch between automatic gear shifting and manual gear shifting in general settings. If you want to shift gears manually, you have to use the (,) and (.) keys.
[*]In the last five seconds of a king challenge, a slight ticking sound starts, which notifies the player that he doesn't have much time left.
[*]The dirt tires now flip automatically to make their running direction face forward.[/list]
[b]Bug fixes[/b][list]
[*]Fixed “Unity editor” being displayed in the top left corner during king challenges. Now, the own Steam name is displayed.
[*]Fixed missing translation in the parts shop. The Undo-button is now correctly called “Undo” instead of “Rückgängig”.
[*]Fixed where, sometimes, the debris of destroyed objects was floating. Now, they should come to rest while lying on the ground.
[*]Fixed floating stones in front of the speed castle bridge.
[*]The Stepper motor tutorial was never ending, and caused the game to be restarted. Now everything works as intended, the tutorial actually ends.
[*]The orbit camera mode now also uses the sensitivity set in the general settings.
[*]Fixed UI having overlapping elements in some screen resolutions.
[*]It was possible to get an immense amount of points in the Stunt Queen, by just driving outside of the map.
[*]When using the stepper motor to power wheels, the car no longer has immense power.
[*]Fixed the terrain collider behind the crash king castle.
[*]The kings and queens don't do any reactions anymore after the challenge has ended.
Stepper motors had some weird behavior, if W, A, S or D was assigned as the actuation key. Now, you cannot assign these four keys anymore since they are used for the driving logic, and thus, these won't interfere anymore with each other.[/list]

We will contiune to improve the game so keep the feedback coming! 

You can either join our [url=https://discord.gg/Tn9dewHvQR ]community discord[/url] and talk directly to us  or you can submit your feedback through our [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1zQUP6rLntFE7jlSxm6BGYLZ85-rYCJwtX1l8ZL2DOoo/edit]Feedback Form[/url].

Have a wonderful Holiday Season and thanks again for playing!

/Creactstudios
